stories.headline: Kishtwar terror attack case: NIA files chargesheet
stories.title: Kishtwar terror attack case: NIA files chargesheet
stories.summary: Jammu, Oct 9: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Friday filed a chargesheet before the NIA Special Court Jammu against an arrested accused and three killed Pakistani terrorists in the Kishtwar terror attack case. In a statement, NIA said it filed the 535-page chargesheet against arrested accused Maneer Ahmed, son of Mohammad Yousuf Koli, resident of Naidgam Chatroo, Inderwal, Kishtwar and three killed terrorists including Saifullah @ Saifullah Kashmiri @ Atiq Nazir @ Atiq Ur Rehman. The chargesheet pertains to the terror attack on 22nd February 2026 at Chatroo, Wani Mohalla, Passer Kote in Kishtwar (RC-03/2026/NIA/JMU). The chargesheet details the conspiracy, the role of the three killed terrorists including Saifullah, a resident of Pakistan and commander of proscribed outfit Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM), and of arrested accused Maneer Ahmed, along with supporting evidence. It charges Maneer Ahmed with voluntarily harbouring and concealing terrorists involved in attacks on security forces and civilians in hilly district Kishtwar under relevant provisions of UA(P) Act, 1967. NIA has also invoked penal section against the accused terrorists for waging war against India and hatching conspiracy from across the border. As per NIA, the attack involved three terrorists led by terror commander Saifullah, affiliated to Kashmir Tigers (Azrael Group), which acts under the proscribed outfit JeM. Retaliatory fire from security forces led to killing of all three. The group, which was active in upper reaches of Kishtwar, was found to have conducted several attacks that resulted in killing of security forces personnel and locals. Arrested accused Maneer Ahmed has been found to be involved in providing support to the group. NIA’s investigation, spanning almost 5 months, has traced the conspiracy to Pakistan. Further investigation in the case is continuing, the agency in a statement said.

stories.headline: Visakhapatnam: Alliance will repeat 2024 election victory in local body polls
stories.title: Visakhapatnam: Alliance will repeat 2024 election victory in local body polls
stories.summary: Bheemunipatnam MLA Ganta Srinivasa Rao expressed confidence that the NDA alliance would repeat its resounding victory in the 2024 general elections in the upcoming local body polls.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bheemunipatnam MLA Ganta Srinivasa Rao expressed confidence that the NDA alliance would repeat its resounding victory in the 2024 general elections in the upcoming local body polls.
Visakhapatnam: Bheemunipatnam MLA Ganta Srinivasa Rao expressed confidence that the NDA alliance would repeat its resounding victory in the 2024 general elections in the upcoming local body polls.

Laying the foundation stone for central median works from Kommadi to Doratota junction at an estimated cost of Rs.10.43 crore at Marikavalasa here on Friday, the MLA mentioned that the people would once again support the alliance, as it fulfilled the promises made during the elections.
Srinivasa Rao stated that the YSRCP would not succeed in its attempts to prevent the local body elections and that the alliance would secure a decisive victory despite any challenges.
Referring to the legal proceedings concerning the conduct of local body elections, Ganta Srinivasa Rao said that the Supreme Court’s verdict had ended attempts to obstruct the electoral process.

He said that the alliance had approached both the High Court and the Supreme Court seeking the implementation of 34 per cent reservation for Backward Classes to enhance their political representation.
He noted that BCs had stood firmly behind the Telugu Desam Party since its inception and assured them that they would continue to receive top priority in the party.
Further, the MLA said that people would not be misled by the statements made by the YSRCP and would exercise their judgement wisely in the local body elections.
He informed that Zilla Parishad elections would be held in Anandapuram, Padmanabham, Bheemunipatnam and Pendurthi mandals.
Highlighting development initiatives in the constituency, Srinivasa Rao revealed that more than Rs 41 crore was spent on various infrastructure projects.
These include 93 road works covering a total stretch of 39 kilometres in the Madhurawada zone.
The MLA said that Visakhapatnam will be beautified and upgraded ahead of the 31st CII Partnership Summit, scheduled to be held on November 12 and 13.

stories.headline: Leading dentists redefining modern dentistry through innovation, impact and excellence
stories.title: Leading dentists redefining modern dentistry through innovation, impact and excellence
stories.summary: Dentistry today extends far beyond traditional clinical care. From advanced implantology and digital orthodontics to cosmetic dentistry, preventive healthcare, and dental education, a new generation of practitioners is reshaping how oral healthcare is delivered and understood.These dentists come from diverse backgrounds and bring different areas of expertise, but they share a common focus on combining clinical knowledge with innovation, patient care, education, and meaningful impact. Their work reflects the evolving face of dentistry, where technology, entrepreneurship, sustainability, and community service are increasingly becoming part of the profession.Dr. Arumalla Sridhar Reddy: Transforming Lives Through Dentistry and Community Service Dr. Arumalla Sridhar Reddy, an Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeon, has made community healthcare a significant part of his professional journey. He has provided free dental health checkups to more than 1.2 million schoolchildren across underserved communities and holds a Guinness World Record for conducting the world’s largest dental health checkup, covering 21,233 students within eight hours.His contributions extend beyond dental care, with Dr. Reddy supporting three orphanage homes that provide care, education, and healthcare to around 250 children.He has also facilitated thousands of free orthognathic surgeries for underprivileged patients and has reportedly received the President of India’s Gold Medal twice for contributions to social service and community welfare.Dr. Shilfa Nigar: Innovating Sustainable DentistryDr. Shilfa Nigar is a practising cosmetic dentist and entrepreneur, building her next chapter around Ecoligners, a dental venture focused on making eco-friendly aligner treatment more accessible and sustainability-conscious. The venture aims to address the waste associated with disposable clear aligners by exploring recyclable solutions and bringing an environmental perspective to modern orthodontic treatment.With nearly a decade of clinical experience, Dr. Shilfa has also been recognised as India’s first General Dental Practitioner to achieve Black Diamond Invisalign Provider status. Beyond dentistry, she has created work-from-home opportunities for around 100 female dentists, enabling them to continue working outside conventional clinical practice.Her journey reflects the intersection of clinical expertise, entrepreneurship, sustainability and social impact.Dr. M. Vijaya Lakshmi Macherla: Crafting Personalised SmilesDr. M. Vijaya Lakshmi Macherla is a dental surgeon, implantologist, and smile designing specialist with 28 years of experience. A first-generation doctor, she began her practice in 2009 with a single dental chair and has since expanded it to three branches in Hyderabad, with a team of doctors and predominantly female staff. Her work in smile designing focuses on creating natural-looking, personalised smiles based on each patient’s facial features, dental needs, and expectations.Beyond clinical practice, Dr. Vijaya Lakshmi has focused on continuous learning with predominantly women-led clinical and support staff. She has also built a social media community of over 3 lakh people, where she shares dental awareness and practical health tips. She has conducted dental camps in government schools and supported free consultations for orphans and physically challenged individuals, along with treatment concessions through social initiatives.Her professional journey also includes advanced training and exposure to international dental programmes, veneers, and digital dentistry, alongside recognition for her contributions to the field.Dr. Prathamesh Kshatriya: Building a New Age Healthcare EcosystemDr. Prathamesh Kshatriya, an oral implantologist and healthcare entrepreneur, has spent nearly eight years studying content, marketing and the psychology behind what makes people pay attention. That experience led him to build Vantage & Cole, a healthcare-focused growth company working with doctors, clinics, hospitals and healthcare brands across positioning, communication, digital growth and market strategy.Kshatriya has also worked behind the scenes as a consultant and growth advisor to healthcare businesses, helping shape how they communicate, position themselves and connect with their audiences. Known for a storytelling style that often gives language to what doctors and students are already thinking or feeling, he has developed a distinctive presence within the healthcare community.Alongside this, he has built Doctors Coach into a community of more than 2 Lakh doctors, dentists and healthcare students, with conversations spanning money, artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship and emerging career opportunities. His work today brings together healthcare, storytelling, media and business.Dr. Prajakta Nawgiri: Transforming Smiles Through Modern DentistryDr. Prajakta Nawgiri is a Cosmetic and Paediatric Dentist and the Founder and Chief Dentist of VISTA Dental, Pune, an award-winning multispeciality dental practice. With over 12 years of experience across Mumbai and Pune, including five years in corporate dentistry, she has treated more than 8,000 patients and built VISTA Dental around clinical excellence, aesthetics and a patient-centric approach.Specialising in cosmetic dentistry and smile designing, Dr. Prajakta focuses on personalised and natural-looking smile transformations. Her practice integrates digital dentistry and advanced dental technology into diagnosis, treatment planning and patient care. Her clientele includes celebrities, entrepreneurs and professionals, with patients travelling from across India and internationally for treatment. A recipient of two FAMDENT Excellence in Dentistry Awards, her journey brings together clinical practice, entrepreneurship and the evolution of a modern, technology-driven dental practice.Dr. Kavita Bhat Kumar: 30 Years of Transforming SmilesDr. Kavita Bhat Kumar is a cosmetic dentist and founder of Designer Smiles, a multispeciality dental clinic in Vile Parle East, Mumbai, which she has led since 1995. With over 30 years of clinical experience, she has built her practice around smile makeovers and aesthetic dentistry, focusing on personalised, natural-looking and conservative treatment. Over the years, her practice has attracted clientele including professionals, models, public figures and patients travelling from overseas for dental care. Her training includes advanced aesthetic dentistry in Germany and specialised education in soft and hard tissue lasers at the University of Bonn.Her approach combines technology with clinical judgement, while giving equal importance to patient comfort and the overall treatment experience. As an Invisalign provider, she incorporates clear aligner therapy into selected cases. Under her leadership, Designer Smiles received the FAMDENT Excellence in Dentistry Award for Clinic of the Year in 2021. She is also a member of the Indian Academy of Aesthetic & Cosmetic Dentistry.Dr. Rachita Guru: Making Dental Education Digital Dr. Rachita Guru is an MDS Orthodontist, Gold Medallist and Invisalign Provider who practises across Gurgaon, Lucknow and Sonipat. She specialises in digital orthodontics, clear aligner therapy and aesthetic smile transformations, while incorporating digital technology into contemporary treatment planning. Her experience as an orthodontic patient during her postgraduate years also shaped her approach to patient education and understanding the questions and concerns people face during treatment.Since starting dental education content during the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Rachita has built an organic social media community of more than 31,000 followers, using digital platforms to make dental science simpler and more accessible. She also conducts courses, webinars and personal branding sessions for dentists. Her work in dental education has earned her the National Icon Award from the Indian Dental Association, and she was also nominated for Social Media Dentist of the Year 2026 at the Famdent Awards.Dr. Naresh Kumar: Advancing Implant Dentistry Through Innovation Dr. Naresh Kumar is a Hyderabad-based prosthodontist and implantologist with more than two decades of clinical experience, specialising in advanced implant dentistry, All-on-X rehabilitation, digital dentistry, and zygomatic implant procedures. As the founder of Vivasmilez Dental, he focuses on complex implant and full mouth rehabilitation cases, combining clinical expertise with evolving digital workflows.Beyond patient care, Dr. Kumar has contributed to dental education and professional development, having trained more than 500 dentists in advanced implant dentistry. Through training programmes, lectures and keynote sessions, he has worked to share his experience and expertise with fellow dental professionals, reflecting the growing role of technology and advanced techniques in modern implantology.Dr. Swati Bharti: Redefining Excellence in Cosmetic DentistryDr. Swati Bharti is a Manipal-trained dentist with more than 25 years of experience, with a clinical focus on root canal treatment, aesthetic and cosmetic dentistry. She is the founder and lead dentist of Rootz Dentz Dental Clinic in Andheri, Mumbai, where she has built an established practice serving more than 3,000 families. Her patient base includes business professionals, NRIs, international patients and a growing number of television personalities and professionals from Mumbai’s entertainment industry.Her work includes smile makeovers, veneers, clear aligners and root canal treatment, with an emphasis on natural-looking outcomes and individualised treatment planning. Dr. Bharti remains closely involved throughout the patient journey, from consultation and clinical planning to post-treatment care and follow-up. Her approach combines aesthetic sensitivity, clinical precision and clear communication, helping Rootz Dentz build long-standing relationships with patients across generations while maintaining a highly personalised approach to dental care.Dr. Shweta N. Lokhande: Championing Preventive and Sustainable Dentistry Dr. Shweta N. Lokhande is a dentist, lecturer, author, global health researcher, oral health educator and certified career counsellor whose work brings together clinical practice, education, public health and community impact. With expertise in global health and research, she advocates for preventive, accessible and sustainable healthcare. As teaching faculty in Community Medicine, she contributes to teaching, mentoring, research supervision, curriculum development, scientific publications and professional preceptorship. Her experience as a registered Dental Care Professional in the UK further informs her perspective on equitable, patient-centred care.Beyond academics and research, Dr. Lokhande promotes engaging, eco-conscious oral health education and community well-being. She also heads the Institutional Forum for Women Empowerment (IFFW), where she works to advance women’s education, confidence, leadership and financial independence. Her contributions have received national and international recognition. Across her varied roles, she continues to combine education, research and advocacy with a focus on creating practical, meaningful change at the grassroots level within healthcare and communities.ConclusionThe journeys of these dentists highlight how the profession is evolving beyond the conventional dental practice. While their areas of expertise range from smile designing and orthodontics to implantology, public health and dental education, each has built a distinct approach to serving patients and contributing to the wider healthcare ecosystem.Together, their stories reflect a broader shift in dentistry towards personalised care, continuous learning, technology-driven treatment and greater public awareness. As the field continues to evolve, these practitioners demonstrate the many ways dental professionals can expand their impact both within the clinic and beyond it.The pages slugged ‘Brand Connect’ are equivalent to advertisements and are not written and produced by Forbes India journalists.

stories.headline: Unprecedented security clampdown in Delhi; 25k personnel deployed, 57 metro stations shut, mobile internet suspended
stories.title: Unprecedented security clampdown in Delhi; 25k personnel deployed, 57 metro stations shut, mobile internet suspended
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 9: An unprecedented security clampdown has been enforced in the Capital ahead of Saturday, after Delhi Police denied permission to the Cockroach Janta Party to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar, with the deployment of 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel, closure of 57 metro stations, suspension of internet services and intensive checks at city's border points, railway stations, bus terminals, hotels and other sensitive locations. According to police, the elaborate security arrangements are aimed at preventing protesters from staging an unauthorised sit-in at Jantar Mantar and to maintain law and order across the city amid the possibility of large-scale mobilisation of people. Internet services will be suspended within a 4-kilometre radius of Jantar Mantar from 10 pm on October 9 to 10 pm on October 10, sources said. The Union home ministry has approved the decision, they said. The suspension will apply to all mobile internet services. Internet services in the rest of Delhi will remain unaffected, they said. The New Delhi district has been divided into 20 zones to strengthen security arrangements and maintain law and order. Each of the 20 zones will be monitored by a Joint Commissioner of Police, a Deputy Commissioner of Police and an Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police to ensure close supervision of the security arrangements, the sources said. Special Commissioners of Police heading various units will also closely monitor the zones and coordinate with senior officers whenever required to respond to any law-and-order situation, they added. Addressing a press conference, Joint Commissioner Nupur Prasad said on Friday that police have denied permission for the proposed October 10 demonstration, citing the short notice given for the event and alleged violations of rules and directions during an earlier protest. She said the application seeking permission for the demonstration was submitted on October 7, just three days before the proposed gathering, adding that according to rules, such applications have to be submitted at least 10 days in advance Police said the application did not meet the stipulated notice period and that the conduct of the July demonstration had raised concerns over compliance with directions issued by authorities. The restrictions have been proposed in view of the Cockroach Janata Party's protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar is facing allegations of voter-list tampering under the guise of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and of bypassing his two colleagues to alter Form 6, a key document to register as a voter. As part of the security arrangements, Delhi Police conducted mock drills at several locations. More than 120 companies of Central Armed Police Forces are expected to be involved in the security arrangements. stories.headline: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?
stories.title: What does a delayed US trade deal mean for India?
stories.summary: A delay in the India-US trade deal adds to the uncertainty that’s already weighing on industry but by itself does not represent a major shock to India’s GDP growth outlook, say economists.“The key issue is not simply the timing of the agreement, but whether the delay results in India facing a materially higher and more persistent tariff disadvantage relative to competing exporters,” says Rajani Sinha, chief economist at CareEdge Ratings.Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, says the lack of a deal is a concern but the impact is hard to quantify.“Impact on exports will be there though not much on GDP as a lot of it is made up by service exports.”Indian goods shipments to the US currently face a 10 percent tariff, plus a most favoured nation (MFN) duty which varies across sectors.The 10 percent levy was imposed on India in July under Section 301 of the Trade Act, where the US cited concerns around forced labour.Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau as FM flags tough road aheadThe rate is far below what Indian goods faced a year ago. Last year, India faced a 25 percent “reciprocal” tariff, which was raised to 50 percent after the US added another 25 percent over purchases of Russian oil.The US and India agreed on a framework for an interim deal on February 6, which cut the rate to 18 percent. Days later, on February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the tariffs US President Donald Trump imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, calling them unconstitutional.Shipments to the US—India’s largest export market, with a 19.8 percent share of outbound shipments—are growing despite the tariffs.Exports to the US rose 6.2 percent to $42.79 billion in April-August this year, according to commerce ministry data, even as talks on a trade deal dragged on. Total merchandise exports jumped 17.9 percent to $215.91 billion over the same period.Last year, front-loading of exports ahead of tariffs had lifted April-June 2025 shipments to the US by 22 percent. A large part of India’s exports to the US such as pharmaceuticals and smartphones remain exempt from tariffs, limiting the damage.Also Read: Nirmala Sitharaman: Global Economy Needs Resilience Amid UncertaintyBut there are worries.President Donald Trump on September 18 signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which authorises tariffs of up to 100 percent on top buyers of Russian energy, India among them.A materially higher tariff under this legislation would represent a significant change in the trade environment and could have much greater implications for Indian exports, investment and growth, says Sinha.Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has, meanwhile, said that both countries have reached “a plateau [on the trade deal] beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult”. This came after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said talks were close to conclusion but that a deal was not “imminent”.Ajay Srivastava, founder of think tank Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), says the statements signal that there could be an interim agreement, instead of a fully fleshed out trade deal.But with tariffs now almost uniform across countries—rather than, for instance, 50 percent on India against 20 percent on Vietnam—“we are relatively better off without a deal”, he says.Also Read: Why India's trade policy makes imports cheaper than manufacturingRisks to IndiaAn immediate risk could come through financial markets and investor sentiment, feels CareEdge’s Sinha.Sinha warned that a prolonged delay, especially if India is seen as losing ground to other emerging market exporters, could hit portfolio flows and the rupee, which is already weighed down by high crude prices, foreign outflows and a strong dollar.Foreign portfolio investors have net-sold Rs 2.3 lakh crore in this calendar year so far, according to NSDL data.The rupee closed Thursday at 96.78 per dollar, near its all-time low of 96.96.Export-oriented firms may become more cautious about expanding capacity in India if access to the US market becomes increasingly uncertain, says Sinha.GTRI’s Srivastava says uncertainty already complicates pricing and contracts. “If US buyers want to enter into long-term contracts with some Indian firm, they may be conservative,” he says.Earlier this week, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said it was “premature” to judge the impact of no deal since it was unclear “which sectors, or to what extent, these tariffs will be applied”, adding that the impact would “obviously” be negative. He also pointed to industry having diversified its exports.“At the same time, we’ve had a number of trade agreements in the past. Many of them have been operationalised, others are in the pipeline… So all these things will mitigate the effect in case there is an additional tariff on some sectors,” Malhotra said at the post-monetary policy press conference.Franziska Ohnsorge, the World Bank Group chief economist for Asia, concurs on the last point, calling India’s recent pacts with the EU, the UK and others “a big deal”.She estimates they have roughly doubled to about 30 percent the share of global GDP to which India has preferential access, and said a US deal would raise it further.Sinha of CareEdge feels India has considerable scope to diversify its trade relationships, and the continued resilience of exports demonstrates that the economy is not excessively dependent on a single market. “Nevertheless, the US remains too important to be replaced quickly.”

opening: A delay in the India-US trade deal adds to the uncertainty that’s already weighing on industry but by itself does not represent a major shock to India’s GDP growth outlook, say economists.

“The key issue is not simply the timing of the agreement, but whether the delay results in India facing a materially higher and more persistent tariff disadvantage relative to competing exporters,” says Rajani Sinha, chief economist at CareEdge Ratings.
body: Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, says the lack of a deal is a concern but the impact is hard to quantify.

“Impact on exports will be there though not much on GDP as a lot of it is made up by service exports.” Indian goods shipments to the US currently face a 10 percent tariff, plus a most favoured nation (MFN) duty which varies across sectors.
The 10 percent levy was imposed on India in July under Section 301 of the Trade Act, where the US cited concerns around forced labour.
The rate is far below what Indian goods faced a year ago.
Days later, on February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the tariffs US President Donald Trump imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, calling them unconstitutional.
A large part of India’s exports to the US such as pharmaceuticals and smartphones remain exempt from tariffs, limiting the damage.
But there are worries.

A materially higher tariff under this legislation would represent a significant change in the trade environment and could have much greater implications for Indian exports, investment and growth, says Sinha.
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has, meanwhile, said that both countries have reached “a plateau [on the trade deal] beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult”.
This came after US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said talks were close to conclusion but that a deal was not “imminent”.
Ajay Srivastava, founder of think tank Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), says the statements signal that there could be an interim agreement, instead of a fully fleshed out trade deal.
Risks to India.
An immediate risk could come through financial markets and investor sentiment, feels Care.
Edge’s Sinha.

Sinha warned that a prolonged delay, especially if India is seen as losing ground to other emerging market exporters, could hit portfolio flows and the rupee, which is already weighed down by high crude prices, foreign outflows and a strong dollar.
Foreign portfolio investors have net-sold Rs 2.3 lakh crore in this calendar year so far, according to NSDL data.
The rupee closed Thursday at 96.78 per dollar, near its all-time low of 96.96.
Export-oriented firms may become more cautious about expanding capacity in India if access to the US market becomes increasingly uncertain, says Sinha.
GTRI’s Srivastava says uncertainty already complicates pricing and contracts.
“If US buyers want to enter into long-term contracts with some Indian firm, they may be conservative,” he says.

Earlier this week, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said it was “premature” to judge the impact of no deal since it was unclear “which sectors, or to what extent, these tariffs will be applied”, adding that the impact would “obviously” be negative.
He also pointed to industry having diversified its exports.
“At the same time, we’ve had a number of trade agreements in the past.

Many of them have been operationalised, others are in the pipeline… So all these things will mitigate the effect in case there is an additional tariff on some sectors,” Malhotra said at the post-monetary policy press conference.
Franziska Ohnsorge, the World Bank Group chief economist for Asia, concurs on the last point, calling India’s recent pacts with the EU, the UK and others “a big deal”.

Sinha of CareEdge feels India has considerable scope to diversify its trade relationships, and the continued resilience of exports demonstrates that the economy is not excessively dependent on a single market.
“Nevertheless, the US remains too important to be replaced quickly.”

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) declined to intervene in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker’s decision to close disqualification proceedings against a group of All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) legislators who had supported C. Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government during the trust vote in May.
The court observed that the Speaker’s decision could not be challenged by an “interloper”.

A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed a plea filed by advocate P.V. Selvakumar, while observing that the sanctity of the constitutional mandate under the Tenth Schedule, which contains the anti-defection law, must be preserved.
“We are fully with you that sanctity of constitutional mandate must be preserved.
But we must understand workings of a democratic system,” the Bench said.

Mr. Selvakumar approached the Supreme Court after the Madras High Court rejected his petition challenging the Speaker’s June 9 decision to drop the disqualification proceedings against the AIADMK legislators.
The Speaker had acted on a May 27 letter from the party’s general secretary seeking withdrawal of the proceedings.
The High Court had held that Mr. Selvakumar, being a third party to the dispute, had no locus standi to interfere in the internal affairs of the AIADMK.
Advocate Nina Nariman, appearing for Mr. Selvakumar, argued that once the Speaker had entertained the disqualification petition, the proceedings ought to have been taken to their logical conclusion.
The legislators, she submitted, had defied the party whip by supporting the government in the confidence vote.

article_sentences: Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani on Friday virtually offered a five-year long term shopping list to the domestic industry to meet the force’s demand as well as acknowledged policy gaps in futuristic technology procurement which he said are being addressed for accelerating the country’s strategic autonomy in an era of disruption.

General Subramani also put forth three asks from the industry on volume, scale, and speed and assured that the relationship between defence forces and the companies is now that of an “industry partner” and not as a vendor.

Speaking at “Annual Session and Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers (SIDM) Champions Award 2026”, the CDS said, “We will give a clear demand signal of over 5 to 7 years and also technology capability signals which have already been done through prospective development programmes.
In order to become better partners, come up with an innovative product that we are compelled to buy or create demand for that, instead of finger pointing over lack of business.”
The General was speaking on one of the sessions on jointness, multi-domain integration and national deterrence, which was moderated by Baba Kalyani, industry veteran and founder president of SIDM.
The CDS stated that long range missiles are the need of the hour and that they are working with the industry to get home grown products.
“We would like to have a missile that fires till 500 km to 600 km first and range can be increased further later,” he put forth the demand.
But, he added a caveat - built it at a cost of less than ₹5 crore so that it’s affordable.
“If you come to us, we will ensure that the industry gets adequate orders.
We require cruise missiles, we require multiple rocket launchers.
Pinaka has a range of 70-80 kms, but today we want to have an extended version of 300-400 kms.

Similarly increase the range of artillery gun ammunition because we cannot change the barrels,” he said, giving a development-cum-manufacturing roadmap to the gathering of representatives of industry, MSMEs and start-ups.

stories.headline: Govt sanctions Rs 603.34 cr incentive for sugarcane farmers
stories.title: Govt sanctions Rs 603.34 cr incentive for sugarcane farmers
stories.summary: The incentive of Rs 709.50 per tonne will supplement the Centre’s Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP), taking the payment to Rs 4,000 per tonne for sugarcane with a sugar recovery rate of 9.5 per cent.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The incentive of Rs 709.50 per tonne will supplement the Centre’s Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP), taking the payment to Rs 4,000 per tonne for sugarcane with a sugar recovery rate of 9.5 per cent.

Chennai: Tamil Nadu has sanctioned Rs 603.34 crore as a special incentive for sugarcane farmers who supplied their crop to mills during the 2025-26 crushing season, Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister M.R.K. Panneerselvam said on Thursday.
Around 90,000 farmers are expected to benefit from the measure, approved on the directions of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.
Payments will be made directly into beneficiaries’ Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, with transfers scheduled to begin from the upcoming Deepavali festival.
For the 2025-26 season, the Centre fixed the FRP at Rs 3,290.50 per tonne for sugarcane linked to a 9.5 per cent recovery rate.
The State’s additional payment will bridge the gap between that amount and the Rs 4,000 price.
Farmers supplying cane with a recovery rate above 9.5 per cent will receive proportionately higher payments, taking their total earnings per tonne beyond Rs 4,000, according to the government.
The assistance will cover growers who supplied sugarcane to the mills that operated during the season.
The government said it had collected farmers’ details, including the quantity of cane supplied, Aadhaar numbers and bank account information, to facilitate identification and payment.
District-level committees headed by Collectors will recommend eligible beneficiaries.
The Directorate of Sugar will scrutinise the recommendations before the incentive is released.
The decision responds to a long-standing demand from sugarcane growers for higher payments and is intended to safeguard their interests, the government said.

sentences.text: Chennai: Tamil Nadu has sanctioned Rs 603.34 crore as a special incentive for sugarcane farmers who supplied their crop to mills during the 2025-26 crushing season, Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister M.R.K. Panneerselvam said on Thursday.
For the 2025-26 season, the Centre fixed the FRP at Rs 3,290.50 per tonne for sugarcane linked to a 9.5 per cent recovery rate.
The incentive of Rs 709.50 per tonne will supplement the Centre’s Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP), taking the payment to Rs 4,000 per tonne for sugarcane with a sugar recovery rate of 9.5 per cent.
